chunks: And it has been narrated that he says, in the sajdah of the obligatory verses of prostration,

"There is no god but Allah, truly, truly. There is no god but Allah, in faith and affirmation. There is no god but Allah, in servitude and bondage. I have prostrated to You, O my Lord, in devotion and bondage, not refusing nor acting arrogantly; rather, I am a lowly servant, fearful, seeking refuge."
Then he raises his head, then says the takbir.

key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: the obligatory Qur'anic verses requiring prostration
key_terms.تَصْدِيقًا: with affirmation and confirmation of truth
key_terms.رِقًّا: in bondage and humility before Allah
key_terms.سَجْدَةِ: the act of prostration, here referring to the prescribed sajdah
key_terms.مُسْتَنْكِفًا: one who refuses or holds back arrogantly

ai.seo_question: What should be said in the sajdah of the obligatory Qur'anic prostration verses?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a supplication to be recited in the sajdah of the obligatory prostration verses. It emphasizes tawhid, humble servitude before Allah, and the etiquette of concluding the prostration by raising the head and saying takbir.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.922 - It has been narrated that in the prostration of the obligatory verses of prostration (Sajdat al-‘Azā’im), one should say:

La ilaha illa Allah haqqan haqqan, la ilaha illa Allah imanan wa tasdeeqan, la ilaha illa Allah ‘uboodiyyatan wa riqqan. Sajadtu laka ya Rabbi ta‘abbudan wa riqqan, la mustankifan wa la mustakbiran, bal ana ‘abdon dhaleelun kha’ifun mustajeer
“There is no god but Allah (swt), truly and genuinely; there is no god but Allah (swt) in faith and affirmation; there is no god but Allah (swt) in servitude and subjugation. I prostrate to You, my Lord (azj), in devotion and humility, without reluctance or arrogance, but as a humble, fearful, and seeking servant.”
Then, he should raise his head and say “Allahu Akbar” (God is Great).
